title.en: Describe the hormones of the adrenal medulla and cortex
Name the hormones of the testis and ovary

say.en: A dog chases you on the way to college. Your heart pounds, your pupils widen, you run faster than ever. In seconds, a gland on top of each kidney has flooded your blood with adrenaline. In this lesson: Describe the hormones of the adrenal medulla and cortex.
Compare insulin and glucagon.
Name the hormones of the testis and ovary.

body.en: Our body has one pair of *adrenal glands*, one at the anterior part of each kidney. Each has a central adrenal medulla and an outer adrenal cortex. The medulla secretes adrenaline (epinephrine) and noradrenaline (norepinephrine), together called catecholamines. They are rapidly secreted in response to stress of any kind and during emergencies, and are called emergency hormones or hormones of fight or flight. They increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection (raising of hair) and sweating, increase the heartbeat, the strength of heart contraction and the rate of respiration, and stimulate glycogenolysis and the breakdown of lipids and proteins. The cortex has three layers: the inner zona reticularis, middle zona fasciculata and outer zona glomerulosa. It secretes corticoids. Glucocorticoids, mainly cortisol, stimulate gluconeogenesis, lipolysis and proteolysis, are anti-inflammatory and suppress the immune response. Mineralocorticoids, mainly aldosterone, act on the renal tubules to stimulate reabsorption of Na+ and water and excretion of K+ and phosphate. The cortex also makes small amounts of androgenic steroids. Under-production of hormones by the adrenal cortex alters carbohydrate metabolism, causing acute weakness and fatigue — Addison's disease.
body.kn: ಅಡ್ರೀನಲ್ ಮೆಡುಲ್ಲಾ ಅಡ್ರಿನಲಿನ್ ಮತ್ತು ನಾರ್ಅಡ್ರಿನಲಿನ್ ಸ್ರವಿಸುತ್ತದೆ — ತುರ್ತು ಹಾರ್ಮೋನುಗಳು. ಕಾರ್ಟೆಕ್ಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಮೂರು ಪದರಗಳಿವೆ. ಗ್ಲುಕೋಕಾರ್ಟಿಕಾಯ್ಡ್ (ಕಾರ್ಟಿಸಾಲ್) ಗ್ಲುಕೋನಿಯೋಜೆನೆಸಿಸ್ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸಿ ರೋಗನಿರೋಧಕ ಪ್ರತಿಕ್ರಿಯೆ ತಗ್ಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಮಿನರಲೋಕಾರ್ಟಿಕಾಯ್ಡ್ (ಅಲ್ಡೋಸ್ಟೀರಾನ್) Na+ ಮತ್ತು ನೀರಿನ ಮರುಹೀರಿಕೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಕಾರ್ಟೆಕ್ಸ್ ಹಾರ್ಮೋನು ಕೊರತೆಯಿಂದ ಅಡಿಸನ್ ರೋಗ.

points.en: Medulla: adrenaline, noradrenaline — fight or flight
Cortex zones (inside → out): reticularis, fasciculata, glomerulosa
Cortisol: gluconeogenesis, anti-inflammatory; aldosterone: Na+ and water retention

caption.en: After a meal blood glucose rises. Beta cells of the islets of Langerhans release insulin, which makes liver and fat cells take up glucose, so the level comes back down. Glucagon from alpha cells does the opposite when glucose is low. Without insulin (diabetes mellitus) glucose stays high and spills into urine. Illustrative model.

body.en: The *pancreas* is a composite gland, acting as both an exocrine and an endocrine gland. The endocrine part is the islets of Langerhans: about 1 to 2 million islets in a normal human pancreas, forming only 1 to 2 per cent of the pancreatic tissue. The main cell types are α-cells, which secrete glucagon, and β-cells, which secrete insulin. Glucagon is a peptide hormone that maintains normal blood glucose: it acts mainly on liver cells (hepatocytes), stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, and reduces cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, so it is a hyperglycemic hormone. Insulin is a peptide hormone that acts mainly on hepatocytes and adipocytes, enhancing cellular glucose uptake and utilisation, and stimulating conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in the target cells, so it lowers blood glucose (hypoglycemia). Prolonged hyperglycemia leads to diabetes mellitus, associated with loss of glucose through urine and formation of harmful ketone bodies; it is treated with insulin therapy.
body.kn: ಲ್ಯಾಂಗರ್‌ಹ್ಯಾನ್ಸ್ ದ್ವೀಪಗಳು ಮೇದೋಜೀರಕ ಗ್ರಂಥಿಯ 1–2% ಮಾತ್ರ. α-ಕೋಶಗಳು ಗ್ಲುಕಗಾನ್ (ರಕ್ತದ ಗ್ಲುಕೋಸ್ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ), β-ಕೋಶಗಳು ಇನ್ಸುಲಿನ್ (ರಕ್ತದ ಗ್ಲುಕೋಸ್ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ) ಸ್ರವಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ದೀರ್ಘಕಾಲದ ಅಧಿಕ ಗ್ಲುಕೋಸ್ ಮಧುಮೇಹಕ್ಕೆ ಕಾರಣ.

body.en: The *testis* has seminiferous tubules and interstitial tissue. The Leydig cells or interstitial cells in the intertubular spaces produce a group of hormones called androgens, mainly testosterone. Androgens regulate the development, maturation and functions of the male accessory sex organs, stimulate muscular growth, growth of facial and axillary hair, aggressiveness and a low-pitched voice, play a major stimulatory role in spermatogenesis, act on the CNS to influence male sexual behaviour (libido), and have anabolic effects on protein and carbohydrate metabolism. The ovary produces estrogen and progesterone. Estrogen is synthesised and secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles. After ovulation the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone. Estrogens stimulate the growth and activities of female secondary sex organs, the development of growing ovarian follicles, the appearance of female secondary sex characters such as a high-pitched voice, mammary gland development, and regulate female sexual behaviour. Progesterone supports pregnancy and acts on the mammary glands, stimulating the formation of alveoli (sac-like structures that store milk) and milk secretion.
body.kn: ವೃಷಣದ ಲೇಡಿಗ್ ಕೋಶಗಳು ಆಂಡ್ರೋಜೆನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು, ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಟೆಸ್ಟೋಸ್ಟೀರಾನ್ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಬೆಳೆಯುತ್ತಿರುವ ಅಂಡಾಶಯ ಕೋಶಿಕೆಗಳು ಈಸ್ಟ್ರೋಜೆನ್, ಕಾರ್ಪಸ್ ಲ್ಯೂಟಿಯಮ್ ಪ್ರೊಜೆಸ್ಟೀರಾನ್ ಸ್ರವಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಪ್ರೊಜೆಸ್ಟೀರಾನ್ ಗರ್ಭಧಾರಣೆಯನ್ನು ಬೆಂಬಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

Progesterone supports pregnancy and acts on the mammary glands, stimulating the formation of alveoli (sac-like structures that store milk) and milk secretion. Leydig cells gives testosterone.

problem.en: A person's blood glucose rises sharply after a meal. Trace how the pancreas brings it back to normal. What happens instead several hours after the meal when glucose falls?

steps.en: High blood glucose stimulates β-cells of the islets of Langerhans to secrete insulin.
Insulin acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes, increasing glucose uptake and utilisation and converting glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis), so blood glucose falls.
When glucose falls between meals, α-cells secrete glucagon, which stimulates glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver, raising blood glucose.

answer.en: Insulin lowers glucose after a meal; glucagon raises it when glucose falls
